messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Zero MVPA in pdf report?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Graydon, The histogram in the visual pdf-report shows the last MVPA estimate from the part 2 daysummary csv-report. By default this is the MVPA calculated based on 5 sec epoch and 80% bout criteria. The threshold for this is set with argument mvpathreshold. I see you are comparing it with the part5 output, but those estimates are not used for this histogram.
Best, Vincent

messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Missing valid days in section 4 and 5 output
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent.

I really appreciate you getting back to me. I have thoroughly checked the previous question you referred to as well as other similar discussions, however I believe my issue is different. I have updated my GGIR to 1.10-7, specified exclude firstlast = FALSE, however I am still seeing missing days in part 4 and 5 output. It is not that I am just missing a few of the first and last days, I am often missing 6 out of 7 or completely different days are shown in part 4 and 5 compared to part 2.

Part 4 and 5 often starts with the days that the acti is turned on and/or posted rather than the days the participant wears the acti, then stops at day 7 from that point. These incorrect start dates also results in the sleep log dates being completely mismatched to the Actidata (i.e sleep log day 1 is matched to the day the acti is turned on, not when the participant starts wearing it 5 or so days later). Any thoughts on anything I could try?

Thanks so much for your time,

Steph

messages.subject: GGIR version 1.11-0 on CRAN and new release structure
messages.subject_clean: GGIR version 1.11-0 on CRAN and new release structure
messages.body_plain:
Dear GGIR-users,

GGIR version 1.11-0 is now on CRAN, new updates are listed in the change log <https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=GGIR/news.html>. Thanks Matt for enhancing the visual report, thanks Jairo for assisting with a few of the other updates, and thanks to all of you who reported issues.

New release structure
So far I have created a new GGIR release with every significant improvement to GGIR. This resulted in 18 releases in the past two years. This is not very practical.

>From now onward I aim to reduce the number of CRAN <https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=GGIR> releases to only two or three per year, and to create intermediate releases on GitHub <https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR> only. New features and bug fixes will first be released on GitHub, which creates a time window for identifying and fixing bugs before they end up in the next CRAN release.

This will make CRAN releases more stable and a good starting point for new GGIR users, while GitHub releases will become the place for the latest bug fixes and feature additions.

If possible, please use the GitHub version whenever you can to help spot issues timely before they end up in a CRAN release.

With this new release structure I will use the following version coding.
A.B-C
A only increases with major changes that affect backward compatibility with previous releases.
B increases with every CRAN release
C increases with every GitHub release.

So, the next GitHub release will be 1.11-1, while the next CRAN release will be 1.12-0 integrating all 1.11-x GitHub releases.

To install GGIR from GitHub, do from within R:
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIR")

or

install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("wadpac/GGIR")

To install GGIR from CRAN, do from within R:

install.packages("GGIR",dependencies=TRUE)

or use the RStudio/R toolbar for package installation.

Best wishes,

Vincent

Dear All,

The document https://www.activinsights.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/geneactiv_instruction_manual_v1.2.pdf  states that 'measurements from different recording frequencies and epoch lengths can be compared with suitable scaling'.

Therefore, if some people had worn devices that recorded at 100Hz, some at 50Hz and some at 30Hz, could scaling be used to accurately compare the physical activity levels between these participants, even though their recording frequencies differed?

If so, how could this be achieved using the GGIR package?

Many thanks for any assistance you can provide.

Best wishes,
Leo

messages.body_plain:
That statement is specific to the SVM metric described in that document, because it sums values per time interval.
None of the metrics embedded in GGIR has this characteristic, by which scaling between sampling rates is not needed within GGIR.

Best, Vincent

messages.subject: ENMO_fullRecordingMean, ACC_nightandday_mg_wei - matching day summaries with person summary outputs
messages.subject_clean: ENMO_fullRecordingMean, ACC_nightandday_mg_wei - matching day summaries with person summary outputs
messages.body_plain:
Hi Everyone,

I am new to the GGIR package and while running some preliminary data reduction on a subsample, I have a few queries related to calculation of ENMO_fullRecordingMean (part 2 summary) and ACC_nightandday_mg_wei (part 5 summary) summary metrics.

Specifically, I would like to understand the nuance in calculating both metrics and how they relate to the data reported in the day summaries for parts 2 and 5.

In Vincent van Hees’s response to Stuart Gray’s query (05/10/2019) about the difference between ENMO_fullRecordingMean and ACC_nightandday_mg_wei, Vincent explained that ENMO_fullRecordingMean is “the average day using all available data in the recording minus invalid data (monitor not worn) by first taking the average per time section of the day and then the average of those averages.” In contrast, ACC_nightandday_mg_wei (the weighted average of daily averages) accounts for invalid (imputed) data.

However, in the GGIR documentation (12/04/2019, p. 14), it is stated that ENMO_fullRecordingMean is “the average ENMO over all the available data normalised per 24-hour cycles (diurnal balanced), with invalid data imputed by the average at similar time points on different days of the week.” As I understand Vincent’s response to Stuart, this description is closer to the ACC_nightandday_mg_wei than to ENMO_fullRecordingMean. Thus, I wonder whether ENMO_fullRecordingMean includes or excludes the non-wear time. If someone was able to clarify this, I would appreciate it!

Relatedly, what is the difference between ENMO_fullRecordingMean and AD_mean_ENMO_mg_0-24hr? It seems from comparing the two metrics that the former may be calculated over all available days while the latter is based on valid days only (please see the attached .xlsx file for comparison). Is this correct?

When computing ACC_nightandday_mg_wei based on part 5 day summaries, my numbers don’t seem to match with the part 5 summary output (please see the GGIR_Q1.xlsx file for an example of 3 subjects). Likewise, when computing plain average based on day summary data, my numbers do not add up to the ACC_nightandday_mg_pla. Thus, I am wondering what I may be missing in my calculations based on the day summary output to match the averages provided in part 5 summary. If anyone has had a similar issue, I would appreciate any feedback.

My last question is related to whether the data from valid days only are accounted for in the computation of both metrics if a valid day criterion is specified (day summary outputs suggest that this is the case)? I am defining a valid day as one with at least 16 hours of valid wear time using includedaycrit = 16 argument. If this is the case, then the difference between two summary metrics would be that ENMO_fullRecordingMean excludes the periods of non-wear during valid days, while the non-wear periods within valid days only are accounted for (by imputation) in ACC_nightandday_mg_wei. Is this correct?

Please see my code below.

Thank you very much in advance for your help!

Best,

Dominika

I wondered if it is possible to narrow the definition of a minimum required number of valid hours to a specific time segment during the day? Since I am new to GGIR and am still exploring different options, I wondered if other users may have experience in successfully narrowing the definition of valid wear time to a specific day segment, which they might be willing to share.

Thank you to all the users sharing their experiences and to colleagues who build and maintain this resource.

Best,

Dominika
